NEWS FROM THE BOARD July 2024 NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Tom Dayley - Commissioner Rod Beck - Board Chairman Ryan Davidson - Commissioner It’s one of the biggest, most colorful, and entertaining events in Idaho! The Western Idaho Fair starts August 16 and runs through August 25. This year you’ll see even more rides, more food options, big name concerts, fascinating exhibits, activities for kids, agriculture, 4H projects and much more. Hope to see you there! We look forward to sharing some world class photos of this year’s event in our next newsletter!

# Page 2^page=2
n WONDERFUL SCENES FROM THIS YEAR’S NATIONAL NIGHT OUT National Night Out is a neighborhood focused community event where our law enforcement partners get to interact and enjoy time with families and individuals. It’s a way to bring law enforcement officers and neighbors together under positive circumstances. The annual event happens the first Tuesday in August. This is such a vibrant celebration of community spirit recognizing the local law enforcement community and their contributions in our neighborhoods. Thank you to the Ada County Sheriff’s Office for partnering with Ada County Commissioners and many others for this year’s event. 2

# Page 3^page=3
ADA COUNTY DRUG COURT PROGRAM GRADUATION Changing lives for the better The July 23, 2024 graduation ceremony for Ada County’s successful Drug Court Program was the county’s 149th graduating class. This was also the 92nd graduating class of Drug Court II, and the 33rd graduating class of Drug Court III. With this graduating class of 14, a total of 1,562 individuals have graduated from the Ada County Drug Court. It’s not an easy commitment either - the typical graduate completes Drug Court in 22.08 months. The economic impact of Ada County graduates is now more than $30M. This is a yearly increase in wages of $19,337.70 per person, per year. The average rise in wages per graduate is $9.11 per hour. The economic impact figure does not include the value of community service. Drug Court graduates have performed over 57,000 hours of community service. July’s class donated a total of 568 hours to their Community Service Projects. Congratulations graduates on this successful and life changing milestone! Learn more about the Ada County Drug Court Program https://adacounty.id.gov/blog/ events/ada-county-drug-court- changing-lives-for-the-better-2/ Pictured Left -to- Right: Ryan Davidson, Ada County Commissioner, Rod Beck, Ada County Commissioner (Chairman), Sydney Sterling, Deputy Regional Director – Office of U.S. Senator Jim Risch, Tom Dayley, Ada County Commissioner, Hon. # Page 4^page=4
4 ADA COUNTY VICTIM SERVICES CENTER We are so proud of the new signage at the Ada County Victim Services Center. As you know the facility has been operating continuously in downtown Boise for almost 18 years! 2006 to be exact. This critically important facility is fully staffed 24/7 with trained professionals to help anyone who is experiencing interpersonal violence. Thank you to all our law enforcement and health care partners for making this facility a community asset. Learn more here: https://adacounty.id.gov/victimservices/ DEPUTY LAUREN MONTAGUE IS THE NEW ADA COUNTY SHERIFF’S OFFICE PUBLIC INFORMATION OFFICER Congratulations to Deputy Lauren Montague on being named Ada County Sheriff’s Office (ACSO) Public Information Officer (PIO). Being the primary point of contact for all media issues involving the Sheriff’s Office is no small task. The job requires excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to represent the 800+ person department with poise and professionalism. No matter what time of day or night Lauren is the point of contact on issues and events that require a statement and official information from ACSO. Lauren began her career with the ACSO in 2013 as the Community Relations Officer. Lauren specialized in crime prevention, community outreach and social media. In 2017, Lauren transferred to patrol, where she became a commissioned patrol deputy. Lauren primarily patrolled south Unincorporated Ada County and was also a school resource officer at Lake Hazel Middle School. Lauren spent several years as a member of the Ada Metro Crisis Negotiations Team. In 2022, Lauren transferred to the Court Security team at the Ada County Courthouse. Lauren is an Idaho POST Certified Instructor and teaches at both the ACSO Dual Academy and the Idaho POST Academy. Lauren has been a valuable collaborator on the Ada County External Communications Team and we look forward to working together in the years to come. 4

# Page 5^page=5
SUZANNE ROBERTS 25 YEARS – JULY 12, 2024 Suzanne Roberts has worked with Ada County since July of 1999 when she started working as a Court Clerk at the old Ada County Courthouse. She moved to the Juvenile Courthouse in 2004 and has been working with the Guardianship Monitoring Program since 2010. Her supervisor, Imelda Ramirez shared the following statement “Even in our personal lives it is not often that we get to reach such a significant milestone as a 25th anniversary, and here, it speaks volumes of the individual and the organization – they must both be doing something right. To say that Suzanne is a dedicated and hardworking employee is simply an understatement – she’s more than that. She works with a vulnerable population in our community and does so with kindness, patience, and understanding; the community could not have a better ally. She pours her heart into her work and her colleagues have great respect for her and her work. We congratulate Suzanne on her 25 years with the County.” JAMIE MARTIN 20 YEARS Whether you work in the Courthouse or have visited the Courthouse, chances are you know Jamie. Jamie has been a front counter staple in the Clerk’s Office for 20 years! Over the years, Jamie has been the first point of contact for the community visiting the Clerk’s Office; starting as a civil front counter clerk, to a Lead and most recently, becoming the front counter Supervisor. Her clerk knowledge is untouchable! Not only can she tell you how to process an Agent’s Warrant or an Out of State Subpoena off the top of her head, but she always has an answer to even the most difficult questions. Jamie also has incredible copy and paste skills! She has a heart of gold and genuinely cares about the people her and her staff serve. Jamie is constantly thinking outside of the box to come up with new and better ways of doing things. If she ever starts a conversation with “Okay, hear me out…”, fasten your seatbelts, because you’re in for a wild ride! She recently implemented and organized the Clerk’s Office Shadowing Program, which had huge success and is in the process of being expanding to other areas of the Courthouse. Jamie, thank you for being so helpful, compassionate, and incredibly loyal to the Clerk’s Office for the last 20 years. 5

# Page 6^page=6
CHERYL EAU CLAIRE 20 YEARS Cheryl Eau Claire began her career with Ada County as a clerk in 2004. She moved to the Trial Court Administration Office in 2007 and was promoted to Business Analyst in March 2021. Throughout Cheryl’s career, she has always gone above and beyond in helping the public, and her co-workers. In her current position, Cheryl works with the district court’s internal budget and ensures that we are complying with accounting and auditing regulations. Cheryl is a great saver! She always looks for better and more efficient ways to use our funds, and thanks to her we have been able to save money. She engages with our vendors and continues to work to protect public funds. Cheryl is dedicated, caring and resourceful in her job. She always lends a listening ear and can give advice to others when requested. Our office would not be what it is today without her support and dedication. Congratulations, Cheryl on your 20 years!!
